what: End-to-end simulation playbook for the 17-step MANUAL_E2E_VALIDATION.md walk: the entire hook-side surface can be driven WITHOUT a live `claude --debug` session by piping stdin JSON directly into `node dist/cli/aide-memory.js hook <name>`. Input shapes: pre-read/pre-edit `{session_id,cwd,tool_input:{file_path}}`; pre-search `{session_id,cwd,tool_input:{pattern}}`; pre-prompt `{session_id,cwd,prompt}`; post-tool-use-recall/post-remember/post-search `{session_id,cwd,tool_name,tool_input,tool_response:[{type:"text",text:"...[N]..."}]}`; session-start `{session_id,cwd,source:"startup"|"compact"|"resume"|"clear"}`; pre-compact + stop `{session_id,cwd}`. trackRecallPost parses memory IDs from `[N]` patterns in tool_response text — payload format MUST be the array-of-{text} shape Claude Code emits, NOT `{content:[{type:"text",...}]}` (wrong shape produces silent failure). Cannot simulate: the agent's *behavioral* response (does it actually call aide_recall after a nudge?) — that's what a human-driven claude --debug walk adds. But the hook-emit-correct-envelope half is 100% mechanically testable this way. Useful when a user asks "simulate everything autonomously before I walk it manually."
why: Saves ~45 min of manual walk time for every regression check, and catches hook-dispatcher regressions (bad envelope shape, wrong decision:block vs additionalContext) without needing a live Claude Code session. Complements `scripts/hooks/__tests__/e2e-autonomous.sh` which only covers H/J/drift-repair — this captures the full flow.
